title: 11 overlapping status labels with no glossary — `EvidenceTable.jsx` renders draft/submitted/pending/pending_review/pending_confirmation/under_review/approved/active/closed/rejected/archived; `approved` and `active` look identical
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceTable.jsx:150-160`
**Root Cause (original):** `EvidenceTable.jsx` rendered all 11 legacy overlapping labels with color collisions, while the backend `Evidence.model.js` enum had already narrowed to 8 clean states — a frontend/backend status-model drift on top of the original ambiguity problem.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30. `getWorkflowStatusBadge`'s `statusConfig` map now lists exactly the real 8-state enum (draft/submitted/assigned/under_review/needs_revision/closed/expired/archived), each with a visually distinct `colorScheme` (gray/yellow/cyan/blue/orange/green/red/purple — no collisions), with an explicit code comment citing EM-012. Dead branches for pending/pending_review/pending_confirmation/approved/active/rejected are gone. **Residual gap (cosmetic, not blocking):** no `Tooltip` was added per-badge (fix prompt item 3), and no regression test enforcing enum/config parity (item 4) — worth a follow-up, but the core defect (11 overlapping labels, color collisions, drift) is closed.
fixEvidence: `EvidenceTable.jsx:150-160` — `statusConfig` rewritten to the real 8-state enum with 8 distinct colors, confirmed on 2026-08-30 (client-panel HEAD d400be5a, `feature/dev`).

title: No evidence completeness indicator per item — `EvidenceCard.jsx`/`EvidenceTable.jsx` show no indicator of: files attached / expiry set / control mapping present / reviewer assigned
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/utils/evidenceCompleteness.js` (new, shared); `EvidenceCard.jsx`; `EvidenceTable.jsx:101-104,319-333,611-624`
**Root Cause (original):** Neither component computed or displayed a completeness percentage across the four dimensions (files/expiry/mapping/reviewer).
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30. A new shared `computeEvidenceCompleteness(evidence)`/`completenessColor(score)` utility (explicitly commented as shared so the two views can't drift) implements the exact 4×25% scoring from the fix prompt, with one honest adaptation: 'reviewer assigned' has no dedicated Evidence field, so it's derived from workflow status (`assigned`/`under_review`/`needs_revision`/`closed`/`expired` ⇒ true) with a clear comment explaining why, rather than faking a field that doesn't exist. `EvidenceCard.jsx` renders the score with a tooltip listing missing items; `EvidenceTable.jsx` adds a 'Complete' column (colored dot + %) AND the bulk 'Show incomplete evidence only' filter (`showIncompleteOnly` state, lines 101-104,611-624) — all four fix-prompt items delivered. No regression found.
fixEvidence: `src/utils/evidenceCompleteness.js` (shared scoring utility) + `EvidenceCard.jsx:91,238-249` + `EvidenceTable.jsx:101-104,319-333,611-624` (Complete column + incomplete-only filter) — all confirmed present and correctly wired on 2026-08-30 (client-panel HEAD d400be5a, `feature/dev`).

title: Framework coverage formula undisclosed on CoverageScoreCard — percentage shown with no formula explanation; unclear if pending mappings count, one evidence covers multiple controls, or non-applicable controls excluded
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-mapping.controller.js:683-820` (`getCoverageStats`); `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/integration-hub/CoverageScoreCard.jsx`; `control-mapping/ControlMappingContent.jsx:154-155,604-606`
**Root Cause (original):** The scorecard rendered a bare percentage with no breakdown of how it was calculated.
**Status:** FIXED — a genuinely thorough, correctly-wired fix, re-verified 2026-08-30 after pulling latest `vibrantix-backend`/`vibrantix-client-panel` (`feature/dev`). Backend `getCoverageStats`/`getBulkCoverageStats` now return `pending`, `notApplicable`, and an explicit `formula` string ("Coverage = Closed (approved) mapped controls ÷ Applicable controls × 100. Applicable controls exclude any marked Not Applicable in the Statement of Applicability."). `ControlMappingContent.jsx` maps `d.pending`→`pendingControls` and `d.notApplicable`→`notApplicableControls` (lines 154-155) and passes all three plus `formula` into `CoverageScoreCard` (lines 604-606), which now renders the formula text, a "{covered} of {total} applicable controls covered" breakdown, and a "Pending approval: N mapping(s)" line. This fix was implemented together with EM-026 (same backend function) and closes both. No regression found — traced backend → API response → frontend prop wiring end-to-end.
fixEvidence: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-mapping.controller.js:806-819` (formula/pending/notApplicable in response) + `vibrantix-client-panel/.../CoverageScoreCard.jsx:21,31,34` (renders formula/pendingControls/notApplicableControls) + `control-mapping/ControlMappingContent.jsx:154-155,604-606` (correct field-name mapping and prop wiring) — all confirmed present and correctly connected on 2026-08-30 after pulling the latest `feature/dev` on both repos.

title: No mapping history on approved control mappings — Approved Mappings tab shows no record of who approved, when, or what comment was provided; violates ISO 19011:2018 §6.4; A.5.33
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-mapping.controller.js:1395-1426` (`getMappingWorkflowHistory`); `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/control-mapping/ControlDetailsDrawer.jsx:514-521,606-620`; `.../MappingWorkflowPanel.jsx`
**Root Cause (original):** `ApprovedMappingsTable.jsx` showed no per-mapping approver/timestamp/comment and no history component.
**Status:** FIXED — but relocated from the originally-cited `ApprovedMappingsTable.jsx` (citation now stale, not deprecated by an architecture change — just an implementation-location choice). Re-verified 2026-08-30: backend `GET /evidence/mappings/:id/workflow-history` (`getMappingWorkflowHistory`) is real, returning `WorkflowEntry` documents sorted by `changedAt` desc, populated with the actor's name/email and any assignee, exactly matching fix-prompt item 1. On the frontend, Approved Mappings rows route via `onViewDetails` → `ControlDetailsDrawer.jsx`, which has a dedicated 'Approval History' icon button per mapping (line 514-521, explicitly citing EM-015) opening a modal that renders `MappingWorkflowPanel` — using the existing `WorkflowHistoryDisplay` timeline component (actor/action/status/timestamp/comment), matching fix-prompt item 2. Item 3 (inline secondary-line summary in the row itself) was not added — a minor residual gap, not blocking. **Minor new issue noted, not blocking:** `evidenceService.getMappingWorkflowHistory`'s catch block silently returns `{success:true, data:{history:[]}}` on ANY error (network failure, 500, etc.), which would misrepresent a real fetch failure as "no history exists" — worth a follow-up to distinguish error states, but does not affect the happy path this fix addresses.
fixEvidence: `evidence-mapping.controller.js:1395-1426` (real WorkflowEntry-backed history endpoint) + `ControlDetailsDrawer.jsx:514-521,606-620` + `MappingWorkflowPanel.jsx` (History icon → modal → real timeline) — confirmed present and correctly wired on 2026-08-30 (client-panel HEAD d400be5a, backend HEAD 8641818, both `feature/dev`).

title: Removing a control mapping has no confirmation dialog or reason capture — `ControlMappingTable.jsx` Remove button calls `onRemoveMapping` directly with no AlertDialog or reason field; violates A.5.33
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/control-mapping/ControlDetailsDrawer.jsx:164-204,556-604`; `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-mapping.controller.js:460-492` (`archiveMapping`)
**Root Cause (original):** `handleRemoveEvidence` used a plain `window.confirm()` with no mandatory documented reason.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30. `handleRemoveEvidence` now opens a real Chakra `AlertDialog` (lines 556-604, explicitly citing EM-016) with a mandatory reason field gated by `MIN_REMOVAL_REASON_LENGTH`; `handleConfirmRemoveEvidence` passes `removalReason.trim()` to `evidenceService.deleteMapping(mapping._id, reason)`. Backend `archiveMapping` (formerly a hard delete, now a genuine soft-archive) independently re-validates `reason.length >= 20` server-side (defense-in-depth, not just a frontend gate) and persists it to a new `WorkflowEntry` (`entityType: 'evidence_control_mapping', status: 'archived', note: reason`) — fully closing the audit-trail gap A.5.33 is concerned with. All fix-prompt items delivered except the optional cleanup (removing the dead `onRemoveMapping` prop from `ControlMappingTable.jsx`), which is cosmetic. No regression found.
fixEvidence: `ControlDetailsDrawer.jsx:556-604` (AlertDialog + reason gate) + `evidence-mapping.controller.js:464-489` (server-side 20-char min enforcement + WorkflowEntry persistence) — confirmed present and correctly wired on 2026-08-30 (client-panel HEAD d400be5a, backend HEAD 8641818, both `feature/dev`).

title: Same user can map evidence and approve the same mapping — no self-review prevention in `ControlMappingContent.jsx`; user with `evidence.write` + `evidence.approve` can create and immediately approve; violates A.5.3
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-mapping.controller.js:1333-1337` (`updateMappingWorkflowStatus`) now has an explicit self-approval guard: `if (['closed', 'not_applicable'].includes(status) && mapping.mappedBy.toString() === req.userId.toString()) { throw AppError.forbidden('You cannot approve your own mapping — a different reviewer must action this.'); }`. This is enforced server-side, so it cannot be bypassed even though the frontend (`ControlMappingContent.jsx`'s `handleApproveMapping`, lines 285-327) still has no equivalent client-side check/disabled-button — a minor residual UX gap (user sees the Approve button enabled then gets a 403) but the actual security/compliance control is in place.
description:
**Files (original):** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/ControlMappingContent.jsx`; backend mapping approval endpoint
**Root Cause (original):** No check prevented the mapping creator from also being the approver.
**Status:** FIXED (server-side) — see fixEvidence. Recommend also disabling the Approve button client-side for a cleaner UX, but this is no longer a compliance-blocking gap.

title: Evidence requests hardcoded at limit 50 with no pagination — `limit: 50` in `useEvidenceRequests.js`; audit programmes with >50 requests silently drop items; violates Clause 9.2

description:

title: No escalation or automated reminder for overdue evidence requests — no overdue indicator, days-overdue counter, or Send Reminder button; requires EM-006 (dueDate) fix first; violates Clause 9.2
description:

EM-006's dueDate prerequisite is now fixed, and `EvidenceRequestsContent.jsx:259-266` now computes `isOverdue` and renders a red 'Overdue' badge — genuine progress since the original finding. However, no 'Send Reminder' button or automated escalation/reminder job was found anywhere (grepped 'Reminder'/'reminder' across `EvidenceRequestsContent.jsx` and `EvidenceRequestDetailDrawer.jsx` — zero matches) — the escalation half of this defect remains fully unaddressed.

Frontend — EvidenceRequestsContent.jsx / EvidenceRequestDetailDrawer.jsx:

```

title: Needs Revision state has no structured re-submission checklist — `EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx` sends free-text comment only; no checklist of deficiency types; violates ISO 19011:2018 §6.5.4
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx:337-443,673-716`; `vibrantix-client-panel/src/services/aiEvidenceService.js:105-112`; `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/workflow/workflowTransition.service.js:163`

title: Closed review history has no date-range or text search — no filter in `EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx`; reviewers cannot locate a specific prior approval for Stage 2 audit evidence; violates ISO 19011:2018 §6.7
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx:1201-1279,1607-1622`; `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence.controller.js:1113-1148` (`getMyReviewHistory`)
**Root Cause (original):** Text search existed but no date-range filter did.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30. The remaining date-range half is now genuinely implemented: `historyStartDate`/`historyEndDate` state with cross-validated min/max date inputs (lines 1607-1622), sent as `startDate`/`endDate` to `getMyReviewHistory`. Backend `getMyReviewHistory` (explicitly citing EM-021) now filters `WorkflowEntry.changedAt` by the supplied range — scoped to when the reviewer's approval action happened, not the evidence's creation date, a deliberate and correct interpretation of what a reviewer means by 'find the approval I made around this date'. Combined with the already-working text search, both halves of the original defect are closed. No regression found.
fixEvidence: `EvidenceMyReviewsTab.jsx:1269-1270,1607-1622` (date-range UI + query params) + `evidence.controller.js:1132-1145` (real `changedAt` range filter on WorkflowEntry) — confirmed working end-to-end on 2026-08-30 (client-panel HEAD d400be5a, backend HEAD 8641818, both `feature/dev`).

title: No cryptographic hash displayed per evidence version — SHA-256 stored in S3 metadata but never surfaced in `EvidenceVersionsContent.jsx` / `VersionTimeline.jsx`; auditors cannot verify file integrity; violates A.5.33; Clause 7.5.3
description:
**Re-verified 2026-08-27:** STILL OPEN on the frontend (confirmed zero matches for 'checksum'/'sha256' in `integration-hub/EvidenceVersionsContent.jsx` and `integration-hub/VersionTimeline.jsx`) — but the backend situation has improved: `evidence.controller.js`'s `getEvidence` handler now DOES return `files[].checksum.{algorithm,value}` in its JSON response with no field exclusion (verified — it's a normal schema field on `Evidence.files`, not S3-metadata-only as originally documented). The remaining gap is purely a frontend rendering gap, not a backend data-availability gap — a smaller fix than originally scoped.

**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/integration-hub/EvidenceVersionsContent.jsx`, `integration-hub/VersionTimeline.jsx`
**Root Cause:** The checksum is available via the standard evidence API response but neither component fetches/renders it. Auditors requesting chain-of-custody verification cannot verify file integrity from the UI.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
Backend — evidence version endpoint:
1. Include sha256Hash in version response: fetch from S3 via s3.headObject({ Bucket, Key }).Metadata.sha256.

Frontend — EvidenceVersionsContent.jsx:
2. Add "SHA-256" column to the version table.
3. Render as monospace truncated string with copy-to-clipboard button.
4. Tooltip: "SHA-256 computed at upload. Compare with your local file hash to verify integrity."

Frontend — VersionTimeline.jsx:
5. Show hash alongside version timestamp.
```

title: Version diff compares metadata only — file content changes invisible; `FileComparisonTable.jsx` compares fields not file bytes; swapped file attachment shows no change in diff view; violates Clause 7.5.3
description:
**Re-verified 2026-08-30 (flipped back from in_progress to open — no fix landed):** after pulling latest `vibrantix-backend`/`vibrantix-client-panel` (`feature/dev`), confirmed STILL zero matches for 'checksum'/'sha256'/'fileSize'/'mimeType' anywhere in `FileComparisonTable.jsx`, and `evidence-version.service.js`'s `compareVersions` `COMPARE_FIELDS` list is unchanged — files are still only diffed by `fileId` membership (added/removed), never by content hash. No progress since the last run; this defect never had a genuine in-progress fix attempt, so `in_progress` was not an accurate status.

**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/FileComparisonTable.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `FileComparisonTable.jsx` shows field-level diff for metadata (title, description, tags, status) but never compares the actual files between versions. A file-swap attack (replacing an approved PDF with different content while keeping identical metadata) would appear as "no changes" in the diff.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: FileComparisonTable.jsx

1. Add a "Files" section to the diff output.
2. For each file in versionA.files and versionB.files, compare: filename, fileSize, mimeType, sha256Hash.
3. If sha256Hash differs: render prominent warning <Alert variant="destructive">File content changed — this is a different file.</Alert>
4. Backend version comparison endpoint: include file-level metadata (name, size, mime, sha256) in both version snapshots.
```

title: Analytics silently capped at 500 items — `getEvidenceList({ limit: 500 })` in `AnalyticsContent.jsx`; projects with >500 items produce silently incorrect metrics; violates Clause 9.1
description:

No server-side aggregation endpoint is used.

**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/AnalyticsContent.jsx`

For organizations with >500 items, metrics are silently incorrect — the cap is a holdover from a development-time optimization never replaced with server-side aggregation.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**

1. Create backend endpoint: GET /evidence/analytics/summary
   Returns server-side MongoDB aggregation: total by status, coverage %, avg review time, framework breakdown.
   Never paginates — returns aggregate numbers only.

2. AnalyticsContent.jsx: replace getEvidenceList({limit:500}) and getMappings({limit:500}) calls
   with a single GET /evidence/analytics/summary call.

3. Remove all client-side aggregation loops.
```

title: Average review time uses `createdAt→updatedAt` gap, not actual review duration — `updatedAt` changes on every edit, inflating reported review time; violates Clause 9.1
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/AnalyticsContent.jsx:145-156`; `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence.model.js` (`submittedAt`/`reviewedAt`); `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/workflow/workflowTransition.service.js:163-172`
**Root Cause (original):** `avgDays` was computed as `updatedAt - createdAt`, inflated by every edit before review.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30. Real `submittedAt`/`reviewedAt` fields now exist on the Evidence model, set by `workflowTransition.service.js`'s generic transition handler whenever `entityType === 'evidence'` reaches `submitted` (sets `submittedAt`) or `closed`/`needs_revision` (sets `reviewedAt`, overwritten — not set-once — so a revision→resubmit→closed cycle measures the latest gap, not the first). `AnalyticsContent.jsx`'s `avgDays` (explicitly citing EM-025) now filters to `reviewedItems.filter(e => e.submittedAt && e.reviewedAt)` and computes `(reviewedAt - submittedAt) / 86400000` — the exact fix-prompt formula, delivered via the same transition-service change that also fixed EM-002's comment-length enforcement. No backend one-time backfill migration for pre-existing evidence was found (fix-prompt item 5) — older items without both timestamps are correctly excluded from the average rather than skewing it, so this is a completeness gap (fewer historical data points), not a correctness bug. No regression found.
fixEvidence: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/workflow/workflowTransition.service.js:163-172` (submittedAt/reviewedAt anchor points) + `AnalyticsContent.jsx:145-156` (avgDays computed from real reviewedAt-submittedAt gap, filtered to items with both) — confirmed on 2026-08-30 (client-panel HEAD d400be5a, backend HEAD 8641818, both `feature/dev`).

title: Framework coverage formula inflated by non-applicable controls — denominator = total mapping count including non-applicable; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; Annex A SoA requirements
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; ISO 27001 Annex A SoA requirements
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-mapping.controller.js:683-820` (`getCoverageStats`/`getBulkCoverageStats`); `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/integration-hub/CoverageScoreCard.jsx`
**Root Cause (original):** The coverage percentage divided mapped controls by all framework controls including those marked "Not Applicable" in the SoA — no exclusion logic existed anywhere in the calculation.
**Status:** FIXED — re-verified 2026-08-30 after pulling latest `vibrantix-backend`/`vibrantix-client-panel` (`feature/dev`). `getCoverageStats` now resolves real SoA exclusions from `ClientFramework.excludedRequirementIds` (intersected with the active requirement set so a stale/cross-framework id can never over-subtract), and computes `totalControls = activeRequirements.length - excludedSet.size` — non-applicable controls are genuinely removed from the denominator, not just labeled. `covered`/`pending` counts are also filtered to exclude the same set. The response returns `notApplicable: excludedSet.size` and the shared `formula` string (see EM-014, fixed together in the same function). `CoverageScoreCard.jsx` now displays "{notApplicableControls} control(s) marked Not Applicable per SoA (excluded)". This fix also incidentally closed a real PLAC project-scoping gap in the same function (the endpoint previously trusted `req.query.projectId` with no membership check) — a positive side effect, not a regression. No regression found.
fixEvidence: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-mapping.controller.js:716-736,806-819` (real SoA-exclusion-driven denominator, `notApplicable` in response) + `vibrantix-client-panel/.../CoverageScoreCard.jsx:36-37` (excluded-count display) — confirmed correct end-to-end on 2026-08-30 after pulling the latest `feature/dev` on both repos.

The exact query-param shape differs from the fix prompt's suggested `filter=uncovered` convention, but the underlying ask — clicking a gap indicator navigates to the relevant filtered list — is delivered for both halves (framework bars and status/pending badges). No regression found.
fixEvidence: `AnalyticsContent.jsx:299,469` (pending-count drill-down) + `:525,602` (framework coverage bar drill-down) — confirmed clickable and correctly routed on 2026-08-30 (client-panel HEAD d400be5a, `feature/dev`).

title: No last-collection timestamp per connector card — connected connector with no recent collection shows `connected` with no staleness indication; violates A.8.8
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/auto-collectors/AutoCollectorCard.jsx:115,138-142,346-350`; `AutoCollectorsContent.jsx:287,767` (`lastRun` prop sourced from the real scans list)
**Root Cause (original):** No timestamp was shown for when a connector last successfully collected evidence.
**Status:** FIXED — relocated from `AutoCollectorsContent.jsx` to `auto-collectors/AutoCollectorCard.jsx` (component refactor, citation now stale but not architecture-deprecated). Re-verified 2026-08-30: rather than adding a new unused `lastCollectedAt` backend field, the fix derives collection staleness from the connector's real `lastRun` object (`response.data.scans[0]`, an actual, already-persisted scan-job record) — `lastCollectedDays` is computed from `lastRun.createdAt` when `lastRun.status` is `completed`/`completed_with_warnings`. Staleness thresholds match the fix prompt exactly: `isCollectionStale` (>7 days, yellow) and `isCollectionVeryStale` (>30 days, red). title: `firstEvidenceAt` onboarding milestone is a dead field — declared on `OnboardingState` schema but never written by any evidence upload path and never read by `setup-health.service.js`'s score computation
description:
**Checklist row:** §12.1 — Getting-started checklist integration: if the module is a first-run milestone (first framework, first evidence, first audit), it's wired into the onboarding wizard/checklist, with completion persisted.
**Files:** `onboarding-state.model.js:25` declares `firstEvidenceAt: { type: Date, default: null }` on the `OnboardingState` schema, clearly intended to mirror the working `firstScanAt` milestone (cloud posture's first scan). `setup-health.service.js`'s `compute()` function (lines 13-40) only ever reads `state.firstScanAt` (line 35, `if (state.firstScanAt) score += 25;`) — `firstEvidenceAt` is never referenced in the scoring logic at all. A repo-wide search for `firstEvidenceAt` (`grep -rn firstEvidenceAt vibrantix-backend/src`) turns up exactly one hit — the schema declaration itself; no controller or service anywhere in the evidence upload path (`evidence-upload.controller.js`, `evidence.controller.js`) ever sets it.
**Root Cause:** The onboarding data model anticipated evidence upload as a trackable first-run milestone (matching the cloud-posture pattern) but the wiring was never finished on either end — nothing populates the field on first upload, and the score formula never consults it even if it were populated.
**Impact:** A brand-new org's very first evidence upload — one of the platform's own named critical E2E milestones ('new org onboarding → framework activation → first evidence upload → first audit → first report') — produces no persisted onboarding-completion signal and contributes nothing to `setupHealthScore`. Any future onboarding checklist/dashboard UI that wants to show 'you've uploaded your first evidence ✓' has no live data to read; the schema promises this milestone is tracked and it silently is not.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-upload.controller.js` (and/or `evidence.controller.js`'s plain `create`/import path), after the first successful `Evidence.create()` for an org, add: `const OnboardingState = require('../onboarding/onboarding-state.model'); const state = await OnboardingState.findOne({ orgId: req.orgId }); if (state && !state.firstEvidenceAt) { state.firstEvidenceAt = new Date(); await state.save(); const { compute } = require('../onboarding/setup-health.service'); await compute(req.orgId); }`. In `setup-health.service.js`'s `compute()`, add a weighted bonus alongside the existing `firstScanAt` check, e.g. `if (state.firstEvidenceAt) score += 10;` (adjusting `WEIGHTS`/the 100-point ceiling so the total still caps correctly).

title: Evidence workflow transitions share the same unguarded `WorkflowTransitionService._updateEntityStatus` — concurrent reviewer actions on the same evidence record can silently last-write-wins with no optimistic lock
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 8.1 operational planning and control
description:
**Checklist row:** §6.4 — Race conditions on concurrent transitions handled: two actors transitioning the same record concurrently don't produce a corrupted or double-applied state (optimistic locking / version check / atomic update).
**Files:** `evidence.controller.js:763` (`transitionWorkflow`) delegates directly to the shared `WorkflowTransitionService.transition('evidence', ...)`. That service reads `currentState` via a separate, non-atomic lookup (`workflowTransition.service.js:50-86`) well before its final write, then calls `_updateEntityStatus()` (lines 418-463), which executes `Evidence.updateOne({ _id: entityId }, { $set: { status: modelValue } })` with no `status: currentState` (or version) precondition in the filter — the write is unconditional.
**Root Cause:** Same root cause as the policy-management module's identical gap (see `policy-management`'s `PM-CHK-003`, filed against the same shared service) — no optimistic-concurrency mechanism exists anywhere in this shared read-check-write sequence, for any `entityType` it drives, evidence included.
**Impact:** Two concurrent `POST /evidence/:evidenceId/workflow/transition` calls while a record is `under_review` (e.g. an assigned reviewer approving at the same moment an org admin — who can override the assigned-reviewer check — rejects) can both pass the allowed-transition check against the same stale `currentState`, both create a `WorkflowEntry`, and both call `_updateEntityStatus` — the later write silently wins with no conflict signal to either caller. The result is a `WorkflowEntry` audit trail entry that doesn't match the evidence's real, final `status` — an auditor sampling the workflow history could see a transition recorded that the entity's current state contradicts.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Fix once in the shared service rather than per-module: in `WorkflowTransitionService._updateEntityStatus` (`workflowTransition.service.js:418-463`), add the precondition to the filter and check the result: `const result = await Model.updateOne({ _id: entityId, [field]: currentState }, { $set: { [field]: modelValue } }); if (result.matchedCount === 0) { const err = new Error(entityType + ' state changed concurrently — please refresh and retry'); err.statusCode = 409; throw err; }` — this requires threading `currentState` into the call at line 167. Fixing it here closes the gap for `evidence`, `policy`, and every other `entityType` this service drives in one place.

title: Action-level permission gating is essentially absent across the entire evidence-management component tree — only 1 of 114 components (`EvidenceManagementContent.jsx`, gating just the Upload button) uses `PermissionHide`/`PermissionGate`; `EvidenceCard.jsx`'s Archive and Hard-Delete buttons render for every viewer regardless of `evidence.update`/`evidence.delete`
description:
**Checklist row:** §1.2 — RBAC permission gates on every UI action: every create/update/delete/approve button is wrapped in `PermissionGate`/`usePermission`, not just the page-level read gate.
**Files:** A repo-wide grep for `PermissionHide`/`PermissionGate` across `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/` (114 `.jsx` files) returns exactly one hit: `EvidenceManagementContent.jsx:745`, wrapping only the 'Upload Evidence' button in `<PermissionHide permission="evidence.create" allowProjectGrant>`. Every other write surface in the module — confirmed concretely in `EvidenceCard.jsx`, the component rendering every evidence card in every list view — has no gating at all: `handleArchive` (line 197's `onClick`) and `handleDelete` (line 205's `onClick`, calling `evidenceService.hardDeleteEvidence` at line 77) render unconditionally for any viewer who can see the card, i.e. anyone passing the module's blanket `(private)/evidence-management/layout.jsx` gate (`evidence.read` — a read permission, not `evidence.update`/`evidence.delete`).
**Root Cause:** The module relies on a single layout-level `evidence.read` gate for page access and otherwise leaves virtually all write/destructive-action gating to the backend alone — the one exception (Upload) suggests action-level gating was a one-off addition, not a pattern applied consistently across the component tree.
**Impact:** Not a data exposure — this module's backend routes (confirmed extensively in this module's earlier checklist run) correctly require `evidence.update`/`evidence.delete` server-side. But any user with mere `evidence.read` (a realistic grant for a read-only project role, e.g. an external auditor account) sees fully clickable Archive and permanent-delete-triggering buttons on every evidence card, which will fail with a raw error only after they click — the same inconsistent-UX pattern already logged for other modules this session (`PM-CHK-001`, `AA-CHK-003`), but here affecting the module's single most common interaction surface rather than one secondary page.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `EvidenceCard.jsx`, wrap the Archive action in `<PermissionHide permission="evidence.update" allowProjectGrant>` and the Delete/hard-delete action in `<PermissionHide permission="evidence.delete" allowProjectGrant>` (soft-delete/archive uses `evidence.delete` per `evidence.routes.js`'s `DELETE /:evidenceId` route — verify which of Archive/Delete maps to which permission against that route file before applying). Do a pass over the rest of the 114-file component tree for other unguarded `evidence.update`/`evidence.delete`/`evidence.create` actions (e.g. control-mapping approve, evidence-request creation, comment/version actions) using this same fix — this one file is the highest-traffic confirmed instance, not necessarily the only one.

title: Evidence workflow notifications cover assignment only — approval/rejection/needs-revision review decisions never notify the evidence owner; second confirmed instance of the same shared-service gap already logged as PM-CHK-005 for policy-management
description:
**Checklist row:** §5.1 — Key lifecycle events dispatch a notification: assignment, due-date approaching/overdue, approval requested, approval decision, status change — each fires through the standard dispatch pipeline, not an ad hoc or silent path.
**Files:** `evidence.controller.js:763` (`transitionWorkflow`) delegates to the shared `WorkflowTransitionService.transition('evidence', ...)`. A repo-wide grep for `notif`/`Notif` in `evidence.controller.js` itself returns nothing — evidence has no notification logic of its own. The shared service's only dispatch (`workflowTransition.service.js:226-271`) is gated to `if (['assigned', 're-assign'].includes(targetState) && opts.assignedTo)` — evidence's own `under_review → closed` (approved) and `under_review → needs_revision` (rejected) transitions (per `featureWorkflows.js`'s `evidence` definition) fall through this check entirely. This is the same root cause already logged as `PM-CHK-005` for policy-management — filed separately here because it's evidence's own review-decision surface that's silent, not a duplicate of that finding.
**Root Cause:** Same as `PM-CHK-005` — only the assignment event was ever wired to the notification pipeline in the shared `WorkflowTransitionService`; the approval-decision event was never added for any entity type it drives.
**Impact:** An evidence uploader is notified when a reviewer is assigned to their submission, but never learns — except by manually reopening the record — that their evidence was approved or rejected/sent back for revision. For evidence specifically, this also means a rejected upload (which per this module's own review cycle needs the uploader to act, e.g. resubmit) generates no prompt to do so.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Same fix as `PM-CHK-005` — one shared-service fix closes both. In `workflowTransition.service.js`, add a decision-notification dispatch alongside the existing assignment one, covering `evidence`'s `closed`/`needs_revision` targets the same way it would cover `policy`'s `active`/`rejected`/`needs_revision`/`archived` — see `PM-CHK-005`'s fix prompt for the exact patch (a generic `_getEntityOwnerId(entityType, entityId)` helper keyed off each entity's `MODEL_MAP` already reused by `_updateEntityStatus`).
